output.contract_title: Vendor Procurement Agreement with Enterprise Partner 003 LLC

clauses.clause_text: Customer shall pay all undisputed invoice amounts within thirty (30) days of invoice date.
Vendor shall notify Customer in writing within twenty-four (24) hours of becoming aware of any confirmed Data Breach.
Each party's maximum aggregate liability shall be strictly limited to the total fees paid under this Agreement in the preceding twelve (12) months.
Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon providing thirty (30) days prior written notice.
This Agreement shall automatically renew for successive two-year periods and CANNOT be terminated for convenience prior to full term expiration.

extraction_notes: Document extracted once for downstream policy comparison

mandatory_requirements.description: Aggregate liability cap must not exceed 12 months of total fees paid or payable.
Customer must have the right to terminate for convenience with no more than 30 days prior written notice.

ambiguities_in_policy: Definition of "total fees paid or payable" for calculating the 12‑month liability cap is not specified (e.g., includes recurring fees, one‑time fees, taxes, discounts?).
Method for measuring "12 months of fees" (calendar months vs. 30‑day periods) is unclear.
Interpretation of "no more than 30 days prior written notice" could be read as exactly 30 days, any period up to 30 days, or a maximum of 30 days; the policy does not clarify which is intended.
What constitutes acceptable "written notice" (email, physical letter, electronic signature) is not defined.

risk_findings.ambiguity_description: The phrase "becoming aware of any confirmed Data Breach" is undefined; criteria for "confirmed" and the point of awareness are not specified, creating uncertainty in compliance timing.
Liability is capped at total fees paid in the preceding twelve months, which may be insufficient to cover potential damages (e.g., data breach penalties) and disproportionately favors the Vendor.

Automatic renewal for two-year periods combined with a clause prohibiting termination for convenience before term expiration conflicts with the earlier termination provision and creates an indefinite commitment without clear exit rights.

inconsistencies.description: Termination clause permits either party to terminate for convenience with 30 days prior written notice, whereas the renewal clause states the agreement cannot be terminated for convenience prior to full term expiration, creating a direct conflict.

Renewal clause mandates automatic renewal for successive two‑year periods, but the contract's defined term is only one year (effective 2026‑01‑01 to expiration 2027‑01‑01), resulting in a chronological inconsistency.

evidence_notes.R002: Clause CLS-0003-LIAB limits each party's liability to fees paid in the prior twelve months, confirming the existence of a potentially insufficient, one‑sided cap.
evidence_notes.R003: Clause CLS-0003-TERM permits termination for convenience with 30‑day notice, while Clause CLS-0003-REN imposes automatic two‑year renewals and prohibits such termination, creating a direct conflict as described.
